    Uint(u64),
    /// A floating""",1)
s=s.replace("""            Self::Int(n) => n.to_string(),
""","""            Self::Int(n) => n.to_string(),
            Self::Uint(n) => n.to_string(),
""",1)
s=s.replace("""                // A u64 beyond i64::MAX is valid JSON; wrapping it would turn
                // it into a negative number.
                Ok(EnvValue::Int(
                    v.try_into().map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?,
                ))
""","""                // A u64 beyond i64::MAX is valid JSON; keep it unsigned rather
                // than wrapping it into a negative number.
                Ok(EnvValue::Uint(v))
""",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cargo check -p shep-core 2>&1 | tail -5

result_text:
Env values above `i64::MAX` now load, up to `u64::MAX`, and are stored as their exact decimal digits. `cargo check -p shep-core` passes; I didn't run the tests or the rest of the gate.

The change is in `crates/shep-core/src/config/app.rs`. I added a `Uint(u64)` variant to `EnvValue`. `visit_u64` now returns it instead of trying to narrow to `i64`, which was the source of the error. `into_string` renders it with `to_string()`.

Negative whole numbers and every other value kind take the same paths as before. Serialization is untouched, so env values are still written as strings.
